item.title: Meta Settles Landmark Teen Social Media Case | Balance of Power: Late Edition 08/26/2026
item.description: "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Mark Zandi, Chief Economist at Moody’s Analytics, says Nvidia is a “juggernaut” and that AI accounts for at least a quarter of economic growth. Zandi thinks AI is already supporting the demand side of the economy and adding modestly to inflation, but clear productivity gains have not yet appeared. Governor Spencer Cox (R-UT) says Meta’s settlement amount should have been much higher, yet argues the more consequential result is the equitable relief requiring child accounts, age-gating, parental controls, algorithm changes, overnight restrictions and healthy pauses. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Fed’s Cook Denies Wrongdoing as Trump Renews Bid to Fire Her
item.description: Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook again denied unproven mortgage fraud allegations repeated by President Donald Trump as he considers whether to renew his effort to remove her, which likely launches another contentious legal battle over the central bank’s independence.
item.dc:creator: Zoe Tillman

item.title: Gov. Cox: Meta Was ‘Losing Badly’ in Court
item.description: Governor Spencer Cox (R-UT) says Meta’s settlement amount should have been much higher, yet argues the more consequential result is the equitable relief requiring child accounts, age-gating, parental controls, algorithm changes, overnight restrictions and healthy pauses. Cox thinks Meta buried research showing significant harms to young users and says Utah will use the money to mitigate those harms, help struggling children, and create more opportunities for them in the real world. Cox believes Meta settled because it was “losing badly” in court. Cox also calls data centers the “physical embodiment” of public concerns about big technology. He speaks with Joe Mathieu and Tyler Kendall on the late edition of Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Zandi: AI Drives at Least 25% of Growth
item.description: Mark Zandi, Chief Economist at Moody’s Analytics, says Nvidia is a “juggernaut” and that AI accounts for at least a quarter of economic growth. Zandi thinks AI is already supporting the demand side of the economy and adding modestly to inflation, but clear productivity gains have not yet appeared. Zandi argues those gains are essential to sustaining company valuations. He also expects Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh’s Jackson Hole speech to be relatively quiet and not market-moving. He speaks with Joe Mathieu and Tyler Kendall on the late edition of Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: SEC Drops Ex-Congressman Insider Trading Case After Trump Pardon
item.description: The Securities and Exchange Commission is dropping its case against a former Republican congressman who was pardoned by President Donald Trump in June after a 2023 insider trading conviction.
item.dc:creator: Nicola M White

item.title: DOJ Fails to Get Steve Bannon’s Contempt Indictment Dismissed
item.description: A federal judge denied the Trump administration’s request to dismiss a contempt of Congress indictment against Steve Bannon, saying the US Justice Department didn’t justify dropping the case after the former White House aide had been convicted and served four months in prison.
item.dc:creator: Jimmy Jenkins

item.title: Alaska Pipeline Aims to Renew Land Rights Early Under Trump
item.description: The owners of the 800-mile Trans Alaska Pipeline System are seeking to renew its federal land authorization more than seven years before it expires, a move that could capitalize on President Donald Trump’s enthusiasm for US oil production.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer A. Dlouhy

item.title: Trump Eases Tariffs on Some Ground Beef Products to Lower Prices
item.description: President Donald Trump signed an order easing tariffs on some ground beef imports, an effort to lower costs for consumers that has managed to rile ranchers and rural state Republicans before the November midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Alicia Diaz

item.title: Russia Preps Escalation, Meta Settles | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 8/26/2026
item.description: Sources close to the Kremlin say Russia is preparing to escalate attacks on Ukraine after concluding that negotiations for a peace deal have reached a dead end. Bloomberg Economics Chief Geoeconomics Analyst Jennie Welch breaks down the latest reporting, and news out of Iran that it agreed to a deal with Oman over the Strait of Hormuz. Then, Chief Investment Officer at Bokeh Capital Partners Kim Forrest helps preview Nvidia earnings dropping after the closing bell. Plus, Bloomberg News Tech Reporter Alexandra Levine and Professor at the University of Florida College of Law Stacey Steinberg explain what comes next after Meta agreed to pay up to $18 billion to settle a lawsuit over teen social media access and exposure. Finally, Lam Research CEO Tim Archer discusses his company's investment for chip research and development expansion. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: What Nvidia's Earnings Signal About the AI Investment Cycle
item.description: Moody's Analytics Chief Economist Mark Zandi says Nvidia's earnings prove that the AI investment cycle is a "juggernaut" and critical to economic growth on "Balance of Power: Evening Edition." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Lula Strikes Deal With Congress to Advance Pre-Election Agenda
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva struck a deal with the heads of Brazil’s Congress to vote next week on a series of bills that could bolster his reelection bid, breaking a months-long stalemate over key government priorities.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Carvalho

item.title: Shapiro Clashes With RFK Jr. After Pennsylvania Measles Deaths
item.description: Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro blamed US Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. for sowing distrust in vaccines as the state confronts a widening measles outbreak that has killed two people and infected hundreds of others.
item.dc:creator: Liz Skalka and Jessica Nix

item.title: Newsom Announces Maritime Grants, Bemoans Shipyard Permit Delays
item.description: California Governor Gavin Newsom announced $48.5 million in grants to support California’s maritime industry and implored a local county board to support a proposal that would speed a massive new shipyard and innovation hub.
item.dc:creator: Alicia Clanton and Laura Curtis

item.title: Republicans’ Unusual Midterm Convention Is a Political Gamble
item.description: Will spotlighting Trump’s record help Republicans win over the swing voters they need to retain control of the House and Senate?
item.dc:creator: Nancy Cook

item.title: Inflation Muted, Spending Stalls | Radio Balance of Power: Early Edition 8/26/2026
item.description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondents Joe Mathieu and Tyler Kendall discuss the latest from the Trump Administration. On today's show, Groundwork Collaborative Vice President Liz Pancotti, Foreign Policy Adviser to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu Ophir Falk, Stonecourt Capital Partner Rick Davis, Harvard Kennedy School Ash Center Visiting Democracy Fellow Jeanne Sheehan Zaino and former Republican Congressman Patrick McHeny. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Moves to Ban Some Foreign Energy Equipment From Grid
item.description: President Donald Trump on Wednesday signed an emergency order that aims to keep some foreign-made transformers and other critical energy equipment out of the nation’s electric grids on national security grounds.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer A. Dlouhy

item.title: Canada-US Relations Set to Get Rockier, Former Trade Negotiator Verhuel Warns
item.description: Canada’s former chief trade negotiator said the country’s relationship with the US will likely get even more precarious before it gets better.
item.dc:creator: Nojoud Al Mallees

item.title: 'Complicated' for Politicians to Paint Positive Economic Picture, Says Patrick McHenry
item.description: Former Republican Congressman from North Carolina Patrick McHenry said that its 'complicated' for politicians to try and paint a positive picture of the US economy during midterm campaigning as voters contend with inflation and higher energy prices. McHenry said that it is unlikely for congress to act on reducing the US debt, because politicians on both sides don't really care about reducing spending. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Democrats Renew Push to Stop Trump Bid to Curb Mail Ballots
item.description: Democrats made a fresh push to keep President Donald Trump from using the US Postal Service to curb mail-in voting this year in a multifaceted legal fight likely to move swiftly back to the Supreme Court.
item.dc:creator: Greg Stohr and Zoe Tillman

item.title: Putin Moves to Escalate War in Ukraine as Talks at Dead End
item.description: Russia is preparing to escalate attacks on Ukraine after concluding that negotiations for a peace deal have reached a dead end, according to three people close to the Kremlin.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News
